title: What is given and what is kept
odia:
ଦେଇଚୁ ଯାହା ପରଲୋକକୁ
ଥୋଇଚୁ ଯାହା ପରଲୋକକୁ।
literal_meaning: What you have given is for the next world; what you have kept is for other people. [Editorial wordplay reading of the repeated ପରଲୋକକୁ.]
meaning_odia: ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଏକେ ପରଲୋକକୁ ଶବ୍ଦ ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରଥମଟି ପରଲୋକ ବା ଆରପାରି, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟଟି ପର ଲୋକ ବା ଅନ୍ୟ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦଖେଳରେ ଦାନର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଓ ସାଇତି ରଖିଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ଅନ୍ୟଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ରହିଯିବାର ଭାବକୁ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏହା ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ମୂଳ ଶବ୍ଦ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: The two endings look identical, but can be heard differently: the next world in one line, other people in the next. Read this way, giving carries value beyond possession, while what is stored remains for someone else. This is our editorial interpretation of the verbal contrast, not a verified traditional gloss.
usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion about keeping every possession rather than helping others, someone quotes these two lines and draws attention to their possible double meaning.
cultural_context: The contrast rests on a change of sense within the same sound, ପରଲୋକ. Giving and keeping introduce two possible destinations without changing the written ending. The next-world reference supplies the saying’s religious horizon in this reading.

witnesses.locator: Page25, fifth item beginning ଦେଇଚୁ ଯାହା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Both printed ପରଲୋକକୁ endings retained; extra interword space normalised only. Translation reads next world versus other people as an explicitly editorial pun. No external full-proverb gloss verified. ଏକେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଦୁଇ ଅର୍ଥ ନେବା ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ପାଠର ସଂଶୋଧନ ନୁହେଁ।
